context.text: Tax revenue equals about 26 percent of annual economic output. The top tax rate on earnings is about 44 percent in a typical city, counting regional and local taxes that vary by place, and starts at about 9 times the average wage. The tax rate on company profits is about 26 percent counting regional taxes. The national minimum wage is about 24 percent of the median full-time wage, with higher minimums set by about 60 percent of regional governments. Collective agreements cover about 11 percent of employees. An employer may dismiss most employees at any time without a stated reason, notice, or severance.

events.text: a budget law that cut national tax revenue by about 1.25 percent of annual economic output a year over ten years, mainly by making permanent lower tax rates on earnings and business income that were due to expire, raising the amount of inherited wealth free of tax, and adding deductions for tips and overtime pay through 2028

a repeal of a rule that would have capped the fees large banks and credit unions charge on overdrawn accounts at a low fixed amount or at their cost. By the regulator's figures, about one in six households pay such fees

a bill restoring the right to bargain collectively to national government employees at agencies where orders of the head of government had removed it. By government data, the share of national government employees represented by a union fell from about 56 to about 38 percent in the year the orders took effect

context.text: Tax revenue equals about 34 percent of annual economic output. The top tax rate on earnings is 45 percent, starting at about 2 times the average wage. The tax rate on company profits is 25 percent. The minimum wage is about 62 percent of the median full-time wage. Collective agreements cover about 27 percent of employees. An employer needs a fair reason to dismiss an employee with two years of service, must give notice of about one week per year of service up to twelve weeks, and must make a redundancy payment when cutting the job of such an employee.

events.text: a finance law that raised tax rates on investment gains, added sales tax to private school fees, raised the extra purchase tax on second homes, and replaced a rule that let some long-term residents avoid tax on income kept abroad, raising tax revenue by about 0.15 percent of annual economic output by 2030

a finance law that keeps income tax thresholds fixed for three more years, raises tax rates on dividend, savings, and property income by 2 points, and applies inheritance tax to unused pension savings and to more farm and business assets, raising tax revenue by about 0.35 percent of annual economic output by 2030

a law that protects employees against unfair dismissal after six months of service instead of two years, pays sick pay from the first day of illness, gives workers on variable hours a right to guaranteed hours, limits dismissing and rehiring staff on worse terms, and eases rules on union organizing and strikes. The government estimated that it gives new rights to about 60 percent of workers

context.text: Tax revenue equals about 38 percent of annual economic output. The top tax rate on earnings is about 47 percent, starting at about 4 times the average wage. The tax rate on company profits is about 30 percent counting local taxes. The minimum wage is about 50 percent of the median full-time wage. Collective agreements cover about 49 percent of employees. An employer with more than 10 employees needs a recognized reason to dismiss anyone employed over six months, must give notice of 4 weeks to 7 months depending on length of service, and must first hear worker representatives where they exist.

events.text: a law cutting the tax rate on company profits by 5 points in steps from 2028 to 2032, from about 30 to about 25 percent counting local taxes, and allowing faster deduction of investment costs until 2027. The official estimate puts its cost at up to about 0.25 percent of annual economic output a year

a tax law that permanently cut the sales tax on restaurant meals from 19 to 7 percent and raised the deduction for commuting costs. The official estimate puts its cost at about 0.1 percent of annual economic output a year

a law requiring companies that carry out national government contracts above a set value to give their workers the pay and conditions of the relevant collective agreements. The government counted about 16,000 such contracts a year

context.text: Tax revenue equals about 44 percent of annual economic output. The top tax rate on earnings is about 55 percent, starting at about 13 times the average wage. The tax rate on company profits is about 26 percent. The minimum wage is about 62 percent of the median full-time wage. Collective agreements cover about 98 percent of employees. An employer needs a real and serious reason and a formal procedure to dismiss an employee, must give one to two months' notice after six months of service, and must pay severance of at least a quarter of a month's pay per year of service, with court awards for unfair dismissal capped on a scale.

events.text: an annual budget, passed without a vote on its text, that added a temporary surtax on the profits of about 400 companies with the largest revenue and a minimum 20 percent tax rate on the highest incomes, raising tax revenue by about 0.3 percent of annual economic output

the next annual budget, also passed without a vote on its text, that extended that surtax for a second year to fewer companies and added a 20 percent tax on luxury assets held through family holding companies. An unofficial estimate puts the surtax's yield at about 0.25 percent of annual economic output

a bill setting a minimum annual tax of 2 percent of wealth on fortunes above about 500 times the median household's wealth, passed by the lower chamber and rejected by the upper chamber. A legislative committee estimated its yield at about 0.1 percent of annual economic output, and its author at about 0.7 percent

context.text: Tax revenue equals about 35 percent of annual economic output. The top tax rate on earnings is about 54 percent in a typical region, counting regional taxes that vary by region, and starts at about 3 times the average wage. The tax rate on company profits is about 26 percent counting regional taxes. The minimum wage is about 49 percent of the median full-time wage. Collective agreements cover about 30 percent of employees. In a typical region an employer may dismiss an employee without a stated reason but must give notice or pay of about one week per year of service, up to eight weeks, and larger employers must also pay severance to long-serving staff.

events.text: a law cutting the lowest income tax rate from 15 to 14 percent. The official estimate puts its cost at about 0.15 percent of annual economic output a year, with the savings in amount rising with income up to the second bracket
a budget law that lets businesses deduct the cost of new investment faster. The official estimate puts its cost at about 0.1 percent of annual economic output a year over five years
